name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
title: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
answer: Valuing illiquid tokens covers the problem of putting a defensible number on a digital asset that has no reliable market price. It applies to tokens with thin order books, long lockups, vesting schedules, or transfer restrictions, and to positions large enough that selling would move the price. The work sits between accounting, treasury and audit, because the same token can be carried at different values depending on the standard being applied and the purpose of the valuation.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Valuing illiquid tokens covers the problem of putting a defensible number on a digital asset that has no reliable market price. It applies to tokens with thin order books, long lockups, vesting schedules, or transfer restrictions, and to positions large enough that selling would move the price. The work sits between accounting, treasury and audit, because the same token can be carried at different values depending on the standard being applied and the purpose of the valuation.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The inputs are on chain and off chain. On chain data covers holder concentration, liquidity pool depth, trading history and vesting contracts, usually pulled from block explorers and indexers. Off chain inputs include term sheets, SAFTs, side letters and cap table records that set lockups and transfer rules. Spreadsheets and valuation models remain the working surface, with data feeds and node access feeding them.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners start by asking whether a quoted price exists at all, then whether it is observable in an active market. Where it is not, common approaches include adjusting a quoted price for a liquidity or marketability discount, using the last transaction price with judgement about how stale it is, and building a model from comparable projects or from the cash flows the token is entitled to. Discounts for lockup length and for the size of the holding relative to daily volume are applied and documented. Every assumption is written down, because the number will be challenged.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The valuation has to survive audit and, where relevant, tax authority scrutiny. That means a documented policy, consistent application period to period, and a clear record of the source of each input and the date it was taken. Provenance matters: who supplied the price, whether it came from an exchange, a broker or an internal model, and whether the token is subject to transfer restrictions that a buyer would have to accept. Independence of the valuer and disclosure of conflicts are part of the same file.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more standardised disclosure of how illiquid token holdings are valued, and toward tools that pull liquidity and vesting data automatically rather than by hand. Regulators and standard setters continue to press on fair value measurement and on the distinction between observable and unobservable inputs. As more tokens unlock and more treasuries hold them, the gap between a headline price and a defensible carrying value is likely to stay the central practical difficulty.
